{"type": "paragraph", "text": "今回のドラマで「ある家臣」としてクローズアップされたのは、秀長の有力の家臣のひとりだった吉川平助（松岡広大さん）です。「豊臣兄弟！」の時代考証を務める黒田基樹さんはその著書で、吉川平助について、もとは近江（現在の滋賀県）の長浜の有力商人だった可能性が高いとしています。江戸時代の長浜の有力商人に、平助の同族と伝えられる人物がいます。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/4ce5e5717d14e508bf009b8bd0498d13.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "平助が攻城戦に関わった鳥取城（鳥取市）", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "最初は秀吉（池松壮亮さん）の配下だったといい、ドラマで描かれた天正16年の年末（1589）の数年前から歴史に顔を出し始めます。天正9年（1581）6月、秀吉から日本海に面した但馬国の城崎郡竹野浜（現兵庫県豊岡市）に使者として派遣され、この地の人間を動員し、指揮したとされます。鳥取城（鳥取市）の攻略に関わる水軍の行動で、もともと水運に長けていた人物であることが想像されます。秀長が熊野地域の攻略をすすめた際には、吉川平助が前線の大将となっています。ドラマで平助は「自分は商人の生まれなので、戦働きはできない」と語っていましたが、実際は戦場でも活躍していた人材でした。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "家康も船で運んだ平助"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "天正14年ごろには、徳川家康（松下洸平さん）を紀伊湊から伊勢大湊まで送るという大役も務めています。このことが後日、「本能寺の変（天正10年）の際、平助が家康を海路脱出させた」というエピソードの元になったかもしれません。資産家で町人への金銀の貸付も行っており、史料からは物流や経済に強く、さらに軍事も含めて多方面に才覚のあった人物像が浮かび上がってきます。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/3918b7b177325e5bb888ae76025f57c6-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "ナゾの多い平助の「横領」の罪"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "そうした平助に不正が発覚したのが天正16年12月（1589年）のことです。ドラマで描かれていたとおり、平助は有力な木材の生産地である熊野の山林の管理を担当していました。切り出された材木を大坂に送り、多額の売り上げを得ていたといいます。これが秀吉の知るところとなり、平助は奈良の西大寺で処刑されます。秀長は兄に詫びを入れに行ったのですが、目通りは許されず、右往左往する羽目に。「天下人の弟」が面目丸つぶれの事態になってしまいました。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "一方、本人が斬首されるという大罪のわりに、主君の秀長も平助の家族も罰せられることはなく、平助の家は存続。平助の子供はそのまま家臣になり、２年後の天正18年に熊野那智山権現社を修造した際には二代目吉川平助が奉行を務めています。不思議なことが多い事件なのですが、「横領」にどんな背景があったのはよくわかっていません。"}, {"type": "秀次の企てと秀長の懐事情を絡ませ、ドラマチックに"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "ドラマではこのナゾも多い「家臣の死」に、秀次の募る危機意識と秀長の苦しい懐事情を絡めて巧みに演出しました。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "大仏建立をめぐって諸大名が尽力したことについて、「殿下の力そのものです」と秀次が秀吉を賛美すれば、甥っ子が言ったそばから「心得違いするでない。殿下の力を見せつけるためではなく、世の安寧を願うからこその大仏建立だ」と真っ向から反論する秀長。秀次のワーディングは微妙だったかもしれませんが、諸大名が居並ぶ中で甥っ子に恥をかかせるとは、気配りの人らしからぬ秀長の態度も妙に大人げないような……。とことん、この２人は反りが合わない、ということなのでしょう。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/a35d932d886ad55f68eb65a76be7200c.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "秀長への不信感を露わにする秀次"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "熊野からの木材調達業務に手を挙げた秀次ですが、その仕事も秀長マターに。基本的に弟の秀長を重用する秀吉の姿勢は、秀次を常に不安にさせていました。元養父で信頼する宮部継潤（ドンペイさん）には、「いつか殿下のようになりたい」と秀吉に対する深い敬意の念を表す一方で、秀長については「疎まれている。何かと目の敵にされる。殿下と近しくなることが気に入らないのかもしれない」と不信感を露わにしました。さらに「いつか用済みとなってどこかに放り出せれるかもしれない」と不安な思いを打ち明けます。その「不安」は正解だったわけですが…。"}, article_text:
豊臣家の軋み、劇的に描く

大河ドラマ「豊臣兄弟！」第44回はそのタイトル通り、史実に残る秀長（仲野太賀さん）の家臣の不祥事をモチーフに扱い、その背景に秀次（山田涼介さん）の思惑と兄弟の世界観の食い違いを浮かび上がらせました。天下一統をほぼ成し遂げた段階で、早くも将来への不安が立ち込め始めた豊臣家内部の軋みをドラマチックに描きました。

長浜の有力商人の出か、物流に強かった吉川平助

今回のドラマで「ある家臣」としてクローズアップされたのは、秀長の有力の家臣のひとりだった吉川平助（松岡広大さん）です。「豊臣兄弟！」の時代考証を務める黒田基樹さんはその著書で、吉川平助について、もとは近江（現在の滋賀県）の長浜の有力商人だった可能性が高いとしています。江戸時代の長浜の有力商人に、平助の同族と伝えられる人物がいます。

最初は秀吉（池松壮亮さん）の配下だったといい、ドラマで描かれた天正16年の年末（1589）の数年前から歴史に顔を出し始めます。天正9年（1581）6月、秀吉から日本海に面した但馬国の城崎郡竹野浜（現兵庫県豊岡市）に使者として派遣され、この地の人間を動員し、指揮したとされます。鳥取城（鳥取市）の攻略に関わる水軍の行動で、もともと水運に長けていた人物であることが想像されます。秀長が熊野地域の攻略をすすめた際には、吉川平助が前線の大将となっています。ドラマで平助は「自分は商人の生まれなので、戦働きはできない」と語っていましたが、実際は戦場でも活躍していた人材でした。

家康も船で運んだ平助

天正14年ごろには、徳川家康（松下洸平さん）を紀伊湊から伊勢大湊まで送るという大役も務めています。このことが後日、「本能寺の変（天正10年）の際、平助が家康を海路脱出させた」というエピソードの元になったかもしれません。資産家で町人への金銀の貸付も行っており、史料からは物流や経済に強く、さらに軍事も含めて多方面に才覚のあった人物像が浮かび上がってきます。

ナゾの多い平助の「横領」の罪

そうした平助に不正が発覚したのが天正16年12月（1589年）のことです。ドラマで描かれていたとおり、平助は有力な木材の生産地である熊野の山林の管理を担当していました。切り出された材木を大坂に送り、多額の売り上げを得ていたといいます。これが秀吉の知るところとなり、平助は奈良の西大寺で処刑されます。秀長は兄に詫びを入れに行ったのですが、目通りは許されず、右往左往する羽目に。「天下人の弟」が面目丸つぶれの事態になってしまいました。

一方、本人が斬首されるという大罪のわりに、主君の秀長も平助の家族も罰せられることはなく、平助の家は存続。平助の子供はそのまま家臣になり、２年後の天正18年に熊野那智山権現社を修造した際には二代目吉川平助が奉行を務めています。不思議なことが多い事件なのですが、「横領」にどんな背景があったのはよくわかっていません。

秀次の企てと秀長の懐事情を絡ませ、ドラマチックに

ドラマではこのナゾも多い「家臣の死」に、秀次の募る危機意識と秀長の苦しい懐事情を絡めて巧みに演出しました。

大仏建立をめぐって諸大名が尽力したことについて、「殿下の力そのものです」と秀次が秀吉を賛美すれば、甥っ子が言ったそばから「心得違いするでない。殿下の力を見せつけるためではなく、世の安寧を願うからこその大仏建立だ」と真っ向から反論する秀長。秀次のワーディングは微妙だったかもしれませんが、諸大名が居並ぶ中で甥っ子に恥をかかせるとは、気配りの人らしからぬ秀長の態度も妙に大人げないような……。とことん、この２人は反りが合わない、ということなのでしょう。

秀長への不信感を露わにする秀次

熊野からの木材調達業務に手を挙げた秀次ですが、その仕事も秀長マターに。基本的に弟の秀長を重用する秀吉の姿勢は、秀次を常に不安にさせていました。元養父で信頼する宮部継潤（ドンペイさん）には、「いつか殿下のようになりたい」と秀吉に対する深い敬意の念を表す一方で、秀長については「疎まれている。何かと目の敵にされる。殿下と近しくなることが気に入らないのかもしれない」と不信感を露わにしました。さらに「いつか用済みとなってどこかに放り出せれるかもしれない」と不安な思いを打ち明けます。その「不安」は正解だったわけですが…。

兄の無茶ぶりに奔走する秀長、「先立つものを」と平助

急に気が変わり、「大仏建立は自力でやる」と言い出した秀吉。焦るのは秀長です。「大仏建立のため、と力を尽くした諸大名がどう思うか」。大名たちを納得させるため自腹を切り、意を尽くして説得にあたりました。史実でも有力大名を居城の大和郡山城で接待するなど、豊臣家と外部との関係維持に腐心してきたのが秀長。「兄の無茶ぶりを何とか形にする弟」というのは「豊臣兄弟！」の基本のフォーマットでもありますが、日本全国を相手に調整役を果たすとなると巨額の資金が不可欠でした。

さらに全国の街道整備を通じて「商業振興による天下一統の推進」という大きな夢を秀長から聞かされた平助。「何とか殿を助けたい」という思いで材木の売り抜けを実行し、今後の政策遂行のための資金に充てようとした、という筋立ては説得力がありました。

平助が夢見たことを遺書で知り、愕然とする秀長でした。

「互いの姿を見てしまう」 利休の予言が現実に

「兄弟の考えは手に取るように分かる」のは秀吉も同様です。秀長が忠臣を守ろうと「自分も同罪だ」と主張してくることは最初から想定していたでしょう。

あらかじめ平助に、「秀長を処罰することはできない。お前には死んでもらわねばならぬ。秀長は罪をかぶろうとするだろうが、受け入れてはならない」と因果を含めます。忠誠心の強い平助にとっては、「はい」という選択肢しかない状況でした。

叔父だろうがなんだろうが、もう容赦はしないと決めた秀次、このやり取りを秀長にあえて吹き込みます。兄弟の間に大きな楔を打ち込んでやろう、という目論見でした。その狙いどおり、秀長は兄を問い詰めました。

「なぜ平助を助けなかった。無罪にも減刑にもできたはず」。秀吉も一歩も引きません。「天下の道を乱した大罪人だ」と応じます。秀長は「忠臣の平助を守りたかった。自分が罰せられても守らなければならなかった」と食い下がります。「天下人の弟であるお前を罪人になどできるわけがなかろう」という秀吉の言葉をきっかけにして、秀吉と秀長との違いが鮮明に浮かび上がりました。

「威光」を巡る2人の価値観の対立

「それは何のためだ」と厳しく問い詰める秀長です。「わしのためか。豊臣のためか。おのれのためか。兄者はおのれの威光を守りたかっただけだ。そんなくだらんものせいで平助は…」と責める秀長に、「まだそのような甘いことを言っているのか」と秀吉。秀吉にとっても治世の要と考える部分だけに、譲りようもない論点です。「その威光がわしらのためにどれほど必要だったか。お前が一番分かっているだろうに」。

身分も資産も無縁の百姓の出身。その出自のせいで無数の屈辱を味わい、遠回りしてきたのが兄弟です。のし上がるためには実力や財力だけでなく、人をひれ伏せさせる「威光」も同じぐらい重要でした。

官位にこだわり、関白そして豊臣姓。「百姓上がりのくせに」という蔑視を跳ね返すためにはなおさら「威光」が重要でした。そのことをすべての苦楽を共にしていたお前が知らないわけがなかろう、というのが秀吉の思いでした。弟に傷がつけば、せっかく築き上げた豊臣の威光に疑念が生じかねない。そこから危機が訪れるかもしれない、と懸念したのでしょう。

しかしその点こそ、秀長が最も譲れないポイントでした。「その威光を守るために人の命を軽んじるな、と申しているのだ」。幾多の“無駄死”を目の当たりにしてきた秀長です。そうした悲劇を繰り返さないことが「天下一統」を目指した理由でした。天下一統をほぼ手中に収めたというのに、まだ無駄死を繰り返すのか、という秀長の嘆きが言葉になりました。

「平助の死を受け入れてしまえば、わしは兄者のこともおのれの事も許せなくなる。平助を罪人にしたのはこのわしだ。わしのいうことが気に入らぬなら、切腹にでも改易にでもしたらええ」。秀長の覚悟の通告に、秀吉も強い言葉で応じざるを得ませんでした。「お前はわしではなく、平助を選ぶのだな。ならば目通りを禁じる。二度とわしの前にその姿を見せるでない」。これまでも兄弟喧嘩を繰り返してきた二人ですが、今回は「治世」をめぐる哲学の違いだけに、根は深そうです。

「これまで見えなかったものが見えてしまう」

この事態、千利休（吉岡秀隆さん）は予見していました。絶大な権力が豊臣家に集中するなか、兄弟の関係について「もう2人は夢を叶えてしまった」ことが危険なのだ、と見抜いた利休。

利休は秀長に「これまでは天下人という的に向かって、同じ方を向いていた。倒さなければならない敵の方を見ていた。だがそんな敵はもういない。今はお互いを見るようになってしまった。これまで見えなかったものが見えるようになるかもしれません」と警告を発していました。

この時は「兄者の事で知らぬことなどない」と強気を装った秀長でしたが、これから「見えてしまった」兄とどう向き合うのでしょうか。

（美術展ナビ編集班 岡部匡志）

article_text:
The re-release of Ken Russell ‘s controversial epic “ The Devils ” was initially only supposed to be in theaters for one week. However, Warner Bros. Clockwork , which oversaw the restoration, announced that it will extend its run due to “popular demand.”

The film opened last weekend in 350 locations across North America. It grossed over $1.7 million for a per-screen average of $4,925. That’s a respectable result for a re-release.

Clockwork will continue to monitor ticket sales and will keep it in theaters for as long as it keeps performing, according to an individual with knowledge of its release plans. It will be in 315 locations in its second weekend.

The NC-17 film marks the first time that an uncensored director’s cut is available to audiences everywhere. Clockwork premiered the remastered, unabridged version at Cannes and then rolled the film out at key film festivals such as Il Cinema Ritrovato, Toronto International Film Festival, New York Film Festival, Beyond Fest, BFI London Film Festival, Sitges Film Festival, and Festival Lumière.

“The Devils” stars Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed. Its scabrous look at religion, power, and corruption was considered too hot to handle in 1971 (nuns simulating sexual acts with a massive cross had its detractors). Those pesky censors necessitated certain alterations upon release.

But over the decades, the film’s renown has grown and “The Devils” has been championed by movie lovers, such as Guillermo del Toro. The cut was originally reconstructed in 2004 under the supervision of Russell and the film’s editor Michael Bradsell with the collaboration of Mark Kermode and Paul Joyce. The 4K restoration was completed using the original camera negative at WB Water Tower Color, with audio restoration completed using original composite 35mm mag film at WB Sound.

An international theatrical release will follow. BFI will release the film in the U.K/ and Ireland beginning October 30. Theatrical runs will also extend to Poland (October 23), France (October 28), Australia/New Zealand (October 29), Germany/Austria (October 29), Greece (November 12), the Netherlands (November 12), and other territories.
excerpt_original: Clockwork will keep the restored version of the controversial epic in cinemas beyond its one-week engagement.

editorial_title_zh: 皮耶鲁吉奥·安东尼奥奇以意识所见描绘事物
editorial_excerpt_zh: 罗马里希特画廊展出皮耶鲁吉奥·安东尼奥奇的作品：一种源于宁静的绘画，光线与内省颠覆了目光。文章《皮耶鲁吉奥·安东尼奥奇以意识所见描绘事物》来自exibart.com。

"本次展览名为“从静止中培育光明”，在罗马里希特画廊展出至2026年11月20日，本文的灵感源自这样一个问题：当我们停下来时会发生什么？在静止中存在一种深刻的含义，这是一个我们所有注意力清晰而完整地指向某些感受的时刻。与其将这种状态视为一种心理上的自我中心主义，不如说它是一种以不同于我们通常思考的方式去了解感受和思想流动的方式。这一切促使我们把“静止”视为一种能够调和对立面的行为，因为在静止中，我们的思维得到休息，而通过培育光明，我们获得了一种罕见的内在清晰度。", "links": [{"text": "Coltivare la luce da fermi", "url": "https://www.galleriarichter.com/single-post/pierluigi-antonucci-coltivare-la-luce-da-fermi"}, {"text": "Roma", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/roma/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/3-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-Dove-comincia-ciò-che-non-vedo-40x30cm-olio-su-tela-2026-L’ora-dell’aperitivo-20x30cm-olio-su-lino-2026-Dove-la-vita-è-semplice-20x30cm-olio-su-tela-2026-copia.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "皮耶鲁吉奥·安东尼奥奇，《我看不到的地方开始》，40x30厘米，油画于画布，2026年，《鸡尾酒时间》，20x30厘米，油画于亚麻布，2026年，《生活很简单》，20x30厘米，油画于画布，2026年，里希特艺术画廊，罗马，摄影：Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "从这一视角来看，本次展览中展出的绘画，其形象完全脱离了任何自然主义，能够讲述一种特殊的维度，在这种维度中，现实由艺术家的意识呈现并体验，使人们在画作中看到超越单纯形式构建的意义。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "似乎对安东尼奥奇来说，绘画让他能够将周围事物的解释性反转变得可见，仿佛每件作品都是普通现实的精确反面。这是一种内化的过程，揭示了自然——由风景、树木、岩石、河流和山脉组成——预示着一种内在挖掘和揭示的工作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在技术层面，这些作品展现了一种朝两个方向发展的探索，一方面致力于体积构建，另一方面则旨在将色彩、光线以及从蓝色开始的色调渐变所蕴含的空间关系吸收其中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/5-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-Coltivare-la-luce-da-fermi-Installation-view-Galleria-Richter-Fine-Art-Courtesy-Richter-Fine-Art-Rome-Ph.-Credit-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-copia.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Pierluigi Antonucci, 《从静止中培育光明》, 展览现场, Richter Fine Art画廊, 由Richter Fine Art提供, 罗马, 摄影: Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在Antonucci的探索中，关于当代存在与绘画之间关系的反思既紧迫又深刻，即有必要以一种颠倒的视角来生活，从而摆脱一种惯常的感知和诠释自身存在的模式，以一种不同于平常的视角来观察它。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "事实上，与阿布鲁佐乡村的联系并非通过现场写生来确立，而是经过过滤，超越了日常的常态。画面是正面的，略微倾斜和倾斜的，天空轻盈地吞噬着空间，总体占据作品的四分之三或四分之一，房屋的坡屋顶被简化为基本的几何形状，树冠则一棵一棵地绘制出来，而某些地方的裸露土地则与天空融合，仿佛讲述着一种在混乱的手、眼和心的关系中的内在地理。每一幅风景画唤起一种构图原则，让我们产生一种头晕目眩的感觉，仿佛一切尽收眼底，同时捕捉到每一个元素。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/25-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-Dove-comincia-ciò-che-non-vedo-40x30cm-olio-su-tela-2026-Courtesy-Richter-Fine-Art-Roma-Ph.-Credit-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-copia.jpg", "alt": "Pierluigi Antonucci的作品", "caption": "Pierluigi Antonucci, 《我看不到的地方开始》, 40x30厘米, 画布油画, 2026年, 由Richter Fine Art提供, 罗马, 摄影: Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "正是这些几乎荒凉和无人居住的作品，唤醒了我们的想象力和渴望，想要从内部去体验它们。绘画邀请我们缩小自己，穿越它们，从而迷失其中，沉浸在它们所蕴藏的温暖之中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因此，对于Antonucci来说，形式的简化并不会抹杀其意义，反而通过回归一种原始的视觉谦逊，可以发现艺术家的内省领域。因此，一片天空成为了一个空间界限，有助于理解我们意识到的事物与我们所忽视的事物，正如标记该空间的火焰般的痕迹可以是流动的思维细丝。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/24-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-Sabato-nel-villaggio-24x18cm-olio-su-lino-2024-Courtesy-Richter-Fine-Art-Roma-Ph.-Credit-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-copia.jpg", "alt": "Pierluigi Antonucci 作品", "caption": "Pierluigi Antonucci, Sabato nel villaggio, 24x18cm, 油画于亚麻布, 2024, 由Richter Fine Art, 罗马提供, 摄影: Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种方法让人联想到20世纪30年代英国画家Ben Nicholson的风景画作品，不在于形式和技巧，而在于共同的理解绘画是一种对世界的宁静理解，一种生活体验和知识的源泉。参观画廊环境时，显而易见的风景和基本场景的简单性，与标题的珍贵解读相结合，为我们带来意识流，开启了一段关于绘画图像语义的重要时刻。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿布鲁佐的土地不是按照地理地形来识别的，而是作为一张地图，邀请我们环顾四周。因此，放弃了对树、房子、天空、海洋的概念，以一种忽视已知事物的目光重新发现最简单的事物，用新的眼睛和清澈的光。因此，半耕的田野和天空的边缘成为超越土地的感受的隐喻，尽管有明显的物质性，这物质被火加热，刚刚变成灰烬，被灰色的烟雾覆盖。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/14-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-Dove-la-vita-è-semplice-20x30cm-olio-su-tela-2026-Courtesy-Richter-Fine-Art-Roma-Ph.-Credit-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-copia.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Pierluigi Antonucci, Dove la vita è semplice, 20x30cm, 油画于画布, 2026, 由Richter Fine Art, 罗马提供, 摄影: Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这幅画最引人注目并同时让人喜爱的是其缺乏精确性和其破坏性的新鲜感，这两个元素都赋予了整个展览项目最显著的特征。这些搭配保持粗糙和中断，而色调的并置则产生了最意想不到的组合，如同剥落的痕迹，刚刚溶解成新的和弦。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "画家对乡村生活和缓慢节奏的热爱，以及他至今仍生活在其中，使他能够通过基本的形式，几乎像素描一样，将它描绘得纯净。这是因为安东尼奥努奇理解到，根据他的想法，世界是一个复杂的隐喻，因此必须被简化。因此，他提取出既详细又基本的特征，其中内省和回忆在意识中产生，从意识到主题，而不是相反。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "将感知数据置于首位，使我们能够发现画布上的另一个细节：几乎所有作品在某些地方都有不同的厚度和密度，因为艺术家通过连续的叠加，直到图像浮现，就像一种冥想式的吸收过程，其中绘画成为不同深度状态的穿越，最终某物可以浮现并变得可见。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/23-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-La-materia-ricorda-la-luce-resta-12x16cm-olio-su-lino-montato-su-legno-2026-Courtesy-Richter-Fine-Art-Roma-Ph.-Credit-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-copia.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "皮耶鲁吉奥·安东尼奥努奇，《物质记得，光留下》，12x16厘米，裱在木板上的亚麻布油画，2026年，Richter Fine Art画廊，罗马，摄影：Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在这里，一种纯粹出于意愿的独立研究的价值显现出来，无论是因为它起源于一个乡村地区，人们不可避免地回归到真实和本真的事物，还是因为它走的是与当前常规趋势相反和逆流而行的道路。因此，绘画呈现出明显的风格差异，特别是在某些地方，色调似乎摆脱了画家的控制，仿佛是活的、炽热的丝线，根据自主的联想交织在画布上，有时显得自由。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "相反，在最近的作品中，笔触重新组合，稍微回到诗意的形式轨道上，让一幅经过长期沉思、品味、尝试和重试的画布故事以明亮的清晰度浮现，遵循着艺术家沉默的节奏。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/15-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-La-pazienza-della-terra-20x30cm-olio-su-lino-2026-Courtesy-Richter-Fine-Art-Roma-Ph.-Credit-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-copia.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "皮耶鲁吉奥·安东尼奥努奇，《大地的耐心》，20x30厘米，亚麻布油画，2026年，Richter Fine Art画廊，罗马，摄影：Eleonora Cerri Pecorella", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "另一个将展出作品联系在一起的方面是形式的持续开放性，因此紧贴着想象中的礁石的波浪在无限制地破碎，充满“好水”的云朵拥有轻盈、沉重的轮廓，随着飞行而不断变化，如同不断发展的构图。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/7-–-Pierluigi-Antonucci-Coltivare-la-luce-da-fermi-Installation-view-Galleria-Richter-Fine-Art-Courtesy-Richter-Fine-Art-Rome-Ph.-Credit-Eleonora-Cerri-Pecorella-copia.jpg", "text": "这些选择揭示了一种对事物本质的奇妙自信，只有通过一种罕见的反思能力，才能看到世界，从而‘在静止中培育光明’。这种看似被动的行为，使Antonucci能够重新找到滋养自己故土的根源，了解阳光的舞蹈，如倾盆而下的喜悦雨滴，最终在眼中获得罕见的光芒，这是由内而外产生的视野，而非外在的、分散的视野。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
La domanda da cui origina questo scritto, dedicato alla mostra di Pierluigi Antonucci , intitolata Coltivare la luce da fermi , in programmazione alla Galleria Richter di Roma fino al 20 novembre 2026, è racchiusa nell’interrogativo: cosa succede quando ci fermiamo? Esiste un senso profondo nel raccoglimento, come momento in cui tutta la nostra concentrazione è indirizzata, in maniera chiara e integra, verso alcune sensazioni. Lungi dal considerare tale condizione come una forma di solipsismo psicologico, si svela piuttosto come un modo per conoscere il flusso di sensazioni e pensieri secondo un punto di vista ulteriore e diverso da quello da cui siamo soliti ragionare. Tutto ciò spinge a considerare “ lo stare fermi” come l’azione capace di conciliare i contrari, in quanto in posizione di quiete la nostra mente riposa, mentre coltivando la luce si acquisisce una rara limpidezza interiore.

Secondo tale prospettiva, le pitture esposte in questa mostra, possedendo una figurazione del tutto estranea a ogni naturalismo, sono in grado di narrare una particolare dimensione in cui la realtà è posta ed esperita dalla coscienza dell’artista, permettendo di scorgere nei dipinti un senso oltre le semplici costruzioni formali.

Sembra che per Antonucci dipingere gli permetta di rendere visibile una rara inversione interpretativa rispetto a ciò che lo circonda, come se ogni opera fosse l’esatto rovescio della realtà ordinaria. Si tratta di un processo di interiorizzazione capace di svelare come la natura, composta di paesaggi, alberi, rocce, fiumi e montagne, sia presagio di un lavoro di scavo e svelamento interiore.

A livello tecnico, quanto esposto rivela una ricerca orientata secondo due direzioni, l’una rivolta alla costruzione volumetrica e l’altra intesa ad assorbire nel colore, nella luce e nelle gradazioni tonali che partono dal blu, tutte le relazioni spaziali.

È rilevabile nella ricerca di Antonucci una riflessione tanto urgente quanto profonda circa il rapporto tra l’esistenza e la pittura di oggi, ovvero la necessità di vivere la propria vita da un punto di vista rovesciato , quindi sottraendosi a una modalità abituale di percepire e interpretare la propria presenza, osservandola così da una prospettiva diversa da quella ordinaria.

Tant’è che il legame con il paesaggio abruzzese, dove l’artista vive, non viene fissato dal vivo, bensì filtrato, trascendendo la consueta normalità. Le vedute sono frontali, leggermente sbilanciate e oblique, il cielo inghiottisce con leggerezza lo spazio e occupa complessivamente i tre quarti o un quarto dell’opera, i tetti a falde delle abitazioni sono semplificati in elementari forme geometriche, le chiome sono disegnate albero per albero, mentre la terra brulla in alcuni punti si amalgama con il cielo, quasi a raccontare una geografia interiore nella caotica relazione tra mano, occhio e cuore. Ogni veduta, evocando un principio compositivo, ci permette di avere l’impressione vertiginosa d’aver tutto sotto gli occhi, cogliendone simultaneamente ogni elemento.

Sono proprio queste opere quasi desertiche e disabitate, a risvegliare tanto l’immaginario quanto il desiderio di viverle dall’interno. Le pitture ci invitano a rimpicciolirci per percorrerle e così perderci, immergendoci nel tepore che custodiscono.

Ne consegue come per Antonucci la semplificazione della forma non sopprima il suo senso, bensì, ritornando a una primordiale umiltà visiva, è possibile scoprire il terreno introspettivo dell’artista. Pertanto, una porzione di cielo diventa un limite spaziale utile a capire ciò di cui si è consapevoli a quanto invece si ignora, così come le tracce fiammeggianti che segnano tale spazio possono essere piccoli filamenti di pensieri che scorrono.

Questo approccio ricorda i lavori dedicati ai paesaggi degli anni Trenta del Novecento del pittore inglese Ben Nicholson , non tanto nella forma e nella tecnica quanto invece nella comune capacità di intendere la pittura come una serena comprensione del mondo, come esperienza di vita vissuta e fonte di conoscenza. Visitando gli ambienti della galleria, emerge come la semplicità immediata delle vedute e delle scene essenziali, accostata alla preziosa lettura dei titoli, ci doni un flusso di coscienza , aprendo una parentesi di rilevanza sulla semantica delle immagini dipinte.

La terra d’Abruzzo non è riconoscibile secondo una topografia geografica, quanto piuttosto come una mappa mentale che ci invita a guardarci attorno. Ne consegue l’abbandono del concetto di albero, casa, cielo, mare per osservare, con uno sguardo che trascura il risaputo e riscopre le cose più semplici con occhi nuovi e carichi di una limpida luce. Sicché, i campi semi-arati e i lembi di cielo diventano metafore di un sentire che supera la terra, pur nell’evidente fisicità di una materia riscaldata dal fuoco, appena ridotto in cenere e velato dal fumo grigio.

Quanto più colpisce e fa allo stesso tempo amare questa pittura, è la mancanza di esattezza e la sua dirompente freschezza, elementi entrambi che donano il carattere più incisivo all’intero progetto espositivo. Gli accostamenti rimangono ruvidi e intercisi, mentre dall’affiancamento dei toni nascono le combinazioni più inattese, come tracce slabbrate, appena dissolte secondo nuovi accordi.

Il pittore, innamorato della vita di provincia e dei suoi ritmi lenti che tutt’oggi vive, la racconta fino a renderla pura attraverso forme essenziali, quasi schematiche. Ciò avviene in quanto Antonucci comprende come, secondo il suo pensiero, il mondo sia una metafora complessa e così necessariamente da semplificare. Perciò estrae le fattezze tanto dettagliate quanto essenziali, in cui introspezione e ricordo si inverano procedendo dalla propria coscienza al motivo e mai l’inverso.

Dare la massima importanza al dato percettivo ci conduce a scoprire un ulteriore particolare nelle tele: quasi tutte le opere presentano, in alcuni punti, spessori e densità differenti, in quanto l’artista procede per sovrapposizioni successive, fino a lasciare emergere l’immagine, come in un processo di assorbimento meditativo in cui la pittura diventa attraversamento di diversi stati di profondità, dai quali qualcosa può infine affiorare e rendersi visibile.

Ed è proprio qui che si svela il valore di una ricerca autonoma per pura volizione rispetto alle correnti contemporanee, vuoi perché originata in una terra di provincia, laddove si torna inesorabilmente alle cose vere e autentiche, vuoi perché percorre strade alternative e controcorrente rispetto alle consuete tendenze attuali. Tant’è che la pittura presenta diversità stilistiche evidenti, in particolare in alcune punti i toni sembrano sfuggire a un controllo del pittore, come se fossero filamenti vivi e incandescenti che si intrecciano nella tela secondo associazioni autonome, talvolta presentandosi libere.

Diversamente, nelle opere più recenti i passaggi si ricompongono, rientrando di poco nel binario poetico della forma, lasciando emergere, con splendente chiarezza la storia di una tela lungamente meditata, assaporata, provata e riprovata secondo i silenziosi ritmi dell’artista.

Un ulteriore aspetto che accomuna i lavori in mostra è la costante apertura della forma, così le onde spumeggianti a ridosso di uno scoglio immaginario si infrangono senza limiti, le nuvole cariche di “acqua bona” possiedono profili lievi, pesanti, che mutano volando come composizioni in divenire.

Ecco che queste scelte rivelano piuttosto una meravigliosa sicurezza nel vedere le cose come sono e soltanto attraverso una rara capacità di riflessione con cui guardare il mondo è possibile Coltivare la luce da fermi . Questa azione solo apparentemente passiva, consente ad Antonucci di ritrovare le radici che alimentano il terreno della propria terra d’origine, conoscere la danza dei raggi solari, che cadono come una pioggia battente e gioiosa, sino a ricevere una rara luce negli occhi, sintomo di una visione generata dall’interno piuttosto che dall’esterno diffuso e dispersivo.

title_original: ARTnews Awards 2026 Best Thematic Museum Exhibition: “MONUMENTS”
editorial_title_zh: 2026年 ARTnews 奖最佳主题博物馆展览：“MONUMENTS”
editorial_excerpt_zh: 表彰在洛杉矶 MOCA 的格芬当代馆（The Geffen Contemporary at MOCA）与 The Brick 举办的展览。

"https://www.artnews.com/t/monuments/"}, {"text": "The Brick", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/t/the-brick/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "极少有展览能具有定义一个时代的力量，但这正是形容“MONUMENTS”的一种方式。经过十年的筹备，该展览将退役的邦联纪念碑置于通常用于当代艺术的空间中，从而重新定位了这些纪念碑。在 MOCA 的展厅里，这些纪念碑作为雕塑作品直接陈列在展厅地面上——其中许多作品上的涂鸦依然完好保留——而不是像它们先前在公共环境中那样作为高高在上的权威象征被放置在底座上。通过以这种方式展示纪念碑，该展览让参观者体会到这些雕像真正遗产的含义，以及与它们相似的物体如何继续塑造美国社会。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "凭借探讨沉重概念的敏锐策展论点，“MONUMENTS”还将这些作品与当代艺术家的创作进行了精妙的对话，参展艺术家包括贝瑟尼·柯林斯（Bethany Collins）、朱莉·达什（Julie Dash）与达沃恩·泰恩斯（Davóne Tines）、考琳·史密斯（Cauleen Smith）、托克瓦斯·戴森（Torkwase Dyson）、安德烈斯·塞拉诺（Andres Serrano）、马丁·普里尔（Martin Puryear）、诺娜·福斯廷（Nona Faustine）和汉克·威利斯·托马斯（Hank Willis Thomas）等。他们各异的风格手法探讨了纪念碑性、权力以及在公共空间中谁能被铭记等问题。在 The Brick，联合策展人卡拉·沃克呈献了《无人机》（Unmanned Drone）（2023），她将一座退役的斯通沃尔·杰克逊（Stonewall Jackson）骑马雕像拆解，并以碎片化的方式重新焊接在一起，以此作为我们如何拼凑历史碎片以创造新事物的隐喻。综合来看，参观者可以看到当代艺术家如何在我们理解和处理围绕邦联纪念碑所体现的有毒且有害历史的未决辩论中发挥至关重要的作用。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "通过这些雄心勃勃的搭配，“MONUMENTS”展现了艺术机构重塑历史并使其与当下产生富有成效的碰撞的独特能力。作为一场罕见的、一代人难得一见的展览，“MONUMENTS”堪称主题博物馆展览所能达成成就的研究范本。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "***", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "特别表彰：", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "洛杉矶县立艺术博物馆大卫·格芬展厅（David Geffen Galleries at Los Angeles County Museum of Art）开馆首展，于5月4日开幕", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "尽管不是传统意义上的主题展览，但 ARTnews 奖评审团认为，为 LACMA 大卫·格芬展厅揭幕的陈列配得上特别表彰。LACMA 有时备受争议的建筑由彼得·卒姆托（Peter Zumthor）设计，呈现了一个跨越威尔希尔大道（Wilshire Boulevard）的单一楼层，用于容纳该馆的永久藏品。其目的并非呈现单一的艺术史时间线叙事，而是思考当各个时代、地域和风格一同展出时，它们如何能够创造出共同点。这一陈列成功的关键在于该馆 15 个策展部门之间的合作。策展人们的工作为知名作品提供了新的见解，使鲜为人知的作品大放异彩，并呈现出优雅的对照。", "links": [{"text": "ARTnews Awards", "url": Jackson）和莉兹·帕克（Liz Park）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“让我们以繁盛的方式聚集”（“Let Us Gather in a Flourishing Way”），布法罗 AKG 艺术博物馆（2026年3月6日–9月6日）；巡展至得梅因艺术中心（Des Moines Art Center）（2026年10月24日–2027年1月24日）策展人：安德烈亚·阿尔瓦雷斯（Andrea Alvarez）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“一日中的数个永恒：活体材料时代的形态”（“Several Eternities in a Day: Form in the Age of Living Materials”），哈默博物馆，洛杉矶（2026年4月5日–2026年8月23日）策展人：巴勃罗·何塞·拉米雷斯（Pablo José Ramírez），携手杰西·迪蒂利奥（Jessi DiTillio）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阅读更多关于2026年 ARTnews 奖的信息。", "links": [{"text": "Read more about the 2026 ARTnews Awards.", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/p/artnews-awards-2026/"}], "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Recognizing a group show at a museum or nonprofit institution with a strong curatorial point of view or focused on a significant historical period."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“ MONUMENTS ” at The Geffen Contemporary at MOCA and The Brick , Los Angeles (October 23, 2025–May 3, 2026) Curators: Hamza Walker, Kara Walker, and Bennett Simpson, with Hannah Burstein and Paula Kroll", "links": [{"text": "MONUMENTS", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/t/monuments/"}, {"text": "The Brick", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/t/the-brick/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Few exhibitions have the power to be decade-defining, but that is one way to describe “MONUMENTS.” A decade in the works, the show repositioned decommissioned Confederate monuments by placing them in spaces typically devoted to contemporary art. In MOCA’s galleries, the monuments were shown on the gallery floor as sculptural objects—many of them with graffiti still intact—rather than as elevated symbols of authority placed high above on pedestals, as they previously appeared in public settings. In showing the monuments this way, the show gave visitors a sense of what the statues’ true legacy means and how objects similar to them continue to shape US society."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "With a sharp curatorial thesis that tackled a weighty concept, “MONUMENTS” also expertly placed these works in dialogue with the work of contemporary artists, including Bethany Collins, Julie Dash and Davóne Tines, Cauleen Smith, Torkwase Dyson, Andres Serrano, Martin Puryear, Nona Faustine, and Hank Willis Thomas, among others. Their varied stylistic approaches engaged with questions of monumentality, power, and who gets remembered in public spaces. At The Brick, cocurator Kara Walker presented Unmanned Drone (2023), for which she took apart a decommissioned equestrian statue of Stonewall Jackson and welded it back together in a fragmented way that acted as a metaphor for how we might piece together the fragments of history to create something new. Taken together, visitors could see how contemporary artists are essential in helping us navigate and process the unsettled debates around the toxic and pernicious histories that Confederate monuments embody."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Through these ambitious pairings, “MONUMENTS” displayed the unique capacity of art institutions to reframe history and bring it into productive friction with the present. A singular, once-in-a-generation exhibition, “MONUMENTS” is a study in what a thematic museum show can do."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "***"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Special Citation:"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Inaugural Hang of the David Geffen Galleries at Los Angeles County Museum of Art Opened May 4"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "While not a thematic exhibition in the traditional sense, the ARTnews Awards Jury felt that the hang that inaugurated LACMA’s David Geffen Galleries deserved a special commendation. LACMA’s at-times controversial building, designed by Peter Zumthor, presents a single floor spanning Wilshire Boulevard to hold the museum’s permanent collection. article_text:
Recognizing a group show at a museum or nonprofit institution with a strong curatorial point of view or focused on a significant historical period.

“ MONUMENTS ” at The Geffen Contemporary at MOCA and The Brick , Los Angeles (October 23, 2025–May 3, 2026) Curators: Hamza Walker, Kara Walker, and Bennett Simpson, with Hannah Burstein and Paula Kroll

Few exhibitions have the power to be decade-defining, but that is one way to describe “MONUMENTS.” A decade in the works, the show repositioned decommissioned Confederate monuments by placing them in spaces typically devoted to contemporary art. In MOCA’s galleries, the monuments were shown on the gallery floor as sculptural objects—many of them with graffiti still intact—rather than as elevated symbols of authority placed high above on pedestals, as they previously appeared in public settings. In showing the monuments this way, the show gave visitors a sense of what the statues’ true legacy means and how objects similar to them continue to shape US society.

With a sharp curatorial thesis that tackled a weighty concept, “MONUMENTS” also expertly placed these works in dialogue with the work of contemporary artists, including Bethany Collins, Julie Dash and Davóne Tines, Cauleen Smith, Torkwase Dyson, Andres Serrano, Martin Puryear, Nona Faustine, and Hank Willis Thomas, among others. Their varied stylistic approaches engaged with questions of monumentality, power, and who gets remembered in public spaces. At The Brick, cocurator Kara Walker presented Unmanned Drone (2023), for which she took apart a decommissioned equestrian statue of Stonewall Jackson and welded it back together in a fragmented way that acted as a metaphor for how we might piece together the fragments of history to create something new. Taken together, visitors could see how contemporary artists are essential in helping us navigate and process the unsettled debates around the toxic and pernicious histories that Confederate monuments embody.

Through these ambitious pairings, “MONUMENTS” displayed the unique capacity of art institutions to reframe history and bring it into productive friction with the present. A singular, once-in-a-generation exhibition, “MONUMENTS” is a study in what a thematic museum show can do.

***

Special Citation:

Inaugural Hang of the David Geffen Galleries at Los Angeles County Museum of Art Opened May 4

While not a thematic exhibition in the traditional sense, the ARTnews Awards Jury felt that the hang that inaugurated LACMA’s David Geffen Galleries deserved a special commendation. LACMA’s at-times controversial building, designed by Peter Zumthor, presents a single floor spanning Wilshire Boulevard to hold the museum’s permanent collection. The aim was not to present one chronological narrative of art history but to think through how various eras, geographies, and styles can create commonalities when exhibited together. Key to the success of this hang was collaboration among the museum’s 15 curatorial departments. The curators’ work provides new insights into well-known works, spotlights lesser-known ones, and offers elegant juxtapositions.

***

Nominees:

“Into the Time Horizon” at the Nevada Museum of Art, Reno (November 15, 2025 – January 3, 2027) Curators: Apsara DiQuinzio, with Kolin Perry

“If the word we: 59th Carnegie International” at the Carnegie Museum of Art, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania (May 2, 2026–January 3, 2027) Curators: Ryan Inouye, Danielle A. Jackson, and Liz Park

“Let Us Gather in a Flourishing Way” at the Buffalo AKG Art Museum (March 6–September 6, 2026); traveled to Des Moines Art Center (October 24, 2026–January 24, 2027) Curator: Andrea Alvarez

“Several Eternities in a Day: Form in the Age of Living Materials” at the Hammer Museum, Los Angeles (April 5, 2026–August 23, 2026) Curators: Pablo José Ramírez, with Jessi DiTillio

article_text:
Al Museo Civico Archeologico di Bologna è possibile visitare la mostra Elliott Erwitt. L’arte di osservare, curata da Biba Giacchetti – collaboratrice storica di Elliot Erwitt – prodotta da Civita Mostre e Musei in collaborazione con il Settore Musei Civici di Bologna.

È la stessa curatrice a definire l’esposizione non come una semplice retrospettiva, bensì come un «ritratto in movimento». Ciò che da essa affiora è, infatti, la delineazione della trama artistica e umana di un autore capace di muoversi tra sfera pubblica e privata, alternando vita quotidiana a episodi che hanno segnato il Novecento. È in questo continuo passaggio di registro che risiede la singolarità assoluta di Elliot Erwitt: la capacità di mostrare quanto sia labile tale confine, declinato attraverso la sua «arte di osservare».

L’arte di osservare dell’autore appare come delicata e mai invadente, concede allo spettatore il permesso di accedere in modo silenzioso alle differenti situazioni umane: da ritratto della piccola Ellen sul letto, allo storico incontro tra Nikita Khrushchev and Richard Nixon , fino al famoso scatto Matrimonio di Bratsk . La retrospettiva si configura così come un dialogo coerente e armonioso, nel quale le diverse fotografie confluiscono in un unico racconto, dimostrando come i grandi eventi storici e momenti privati siano indissolubilmente legati dallo stesso filo umano.

Una delle fotografie esposte che incarna perfettamente questa poetica è USA, North Carolina, Segregated Water Fountains , scatto diventato simbolo della segregazione razziale negli Stati Uniti tra gli anni Cinquanta e Sessanta del Novecento. L’immagine ritrae un uomo afroamericano intento a bere da un lavello fatiscente, collocato al fianco di una ben più curata fontanella. Sulla parete, le due diciture emblematiche – white e colored – trasformano la fotografia in una testimonianza di un’umanità frammentata dal pregiudizio e prigioniera di assurdi condizionamenti sociali.

Il percorso espositivo, contenente circa cento scatti, si articola in cinque sezioni. Alle immagini che hanno consacrato la fama internazionale del fotografo – dal bacio nello specchietto retrovisore alle fotografie dei grandi della terra – si affiancano fotografie appartenenti alla sua collezione privata, con l’introduzione di alcuni scatti inediti esposti per la prima volta. È interessante, quindi, come all’Elliott Erwitt più noto e amato si accosti una dimensione meno conosciuta della sua produzione, che ne rivela il lato più intimo.

Il fil rouge che attraversa e unifica l’intero progetto è la sua inconfondibile vena ironica. L’ironia di Erwitt si caratterizza per una profonda matrice empatica, in grado di portare alla luce la fragilità, le assurdità e la bellezza intrinseca dell’esistenza. L’intento non è mai derisorio, quanto piuttosto di partecipazione: un modo per rimarcare la comune vulnerabilità dell’essere umano, magnifico nella propria ineludibile e talvolta persino divertente inadeguatezza. La sua ironia, unitamente al già citato intreccio tra la sfera pubblica e quella privata, pervade l’intera mostra: dalla sezione dedicata alle immagini personali, a quella dedicata proprio all’ironia, fino ai ritratti dei cani e alla serie conclusiva degli autoritratti.

All’origine di questa visiona c’è la biografia di uomo autenticamente cosmopolita. Nato nella capitale francese da una famiglia russa emigrata all’indomani della Rivoluzione, cresciuto a Milano e in seguito costretto a fuggire negli Stati Uniti a causa dell’introduzione delle leggi razziali. Pur avendo vissuto gli anni dell’adolescenza in sostanziale solitudine, non ha mai maturato sentimenti di rivalsa, mantenendo un legame d’affetto speciale con l’Italia, paese in cui è ritornato a più riprese. Proprio la relazione con l’Italia è oggetto di un’attenzione particolare all’interno dell’esposizione. Il Paese non viene rappresentato come un semplice contesto scenografico, ma si configura come un terreno di esplorazione e di sperimentazione visiva ed emotiva, come testimoniano le opere in mostra, scattate prevalentemente nella Roma degli anni Cinquanta e in altre località del Paese.

Il percorso espositivo offre così un accesso intimo e inedito sull’universo artistico e personale di Elliott Erwitt. Capace di cogliere con la stessa sensibilità sia la drammaticità degli eventi sia l’ironia della vita quotidiana, il fotografo fonde l’immediatezza dell’intuizione visiva con una profonda riflessione concettuale. È proprio nel perfetto equilibrio tra questi aspetti, solo apparentemente opposti, che si racchiude l’essenza della sua poetica.

article_text:
At Al Riwaq Art Space , Bahraini artist Mayasa Al Sowaidi approaches the journal as a space for recording, revisiting and reworking personal experiences.

At what point does a word become an image? In Bahraini artist Dr Mayasa Al Sowaidi’s solo show, A Journal of Becoming , the distinction is difficult to maintain. Arabic and English move between handwritten notes, stencilled phrases and abstract shapes. A curved fragment might resemble a flower, a comma or something cellular. Stitching becomes drawing, while a cut edge takes on the character of punctuation.

Curated by Gaida Almogren at Al Riwaq Art Space in Manama, the exhibition unfolds across interconnected rooms and outdoor spaces. Four symbols introduce its visual language: an irregular circle, a geometric form resembling a capital I, an asymmetrical quadrilateral and a rounded, flower-like shape. Displayed above an open journal, they suggest an unfamiliar alphabet. As these forms reappear, visitors gradually learn to recognise them.

Trained in mathematics and management, the self-taught artist has long experimented with geometry, collage and collected fragments. Her earlier exhibition The Golden Ratio , in 2023, explored mathematical proportion and visual composition. Here, that underlying structure is continually interrupted. Paintings are cut apart, reconstructed, stitched and suspended, retaining traces of earlier decisions. The journal becomes a place where thoughts remain open to revision.

In All That Came Before , hexagonal canvases establish a geometric order complicated by writing. Handwritten Arabic and English coexist with printed lettering, painted gestures and irregular fabric forms. Some resemble quotation marks; others suggest flowers, bodily forms or cellular membranes. The distinction between image and language becomes increasingly uncertain.

This ambiguity has a history within Arab modernism. Iraqi artist Madiha Umar explored Arabic letterforms as independent abstract compositions in the 1940s, anticipating later developments associated with the Hurufiyya movement. Al Sowaidi’s approach is distinct, but similarly allows language to operate beyond conventional communication.

Bahrain’s bilingual environment adds another dimension. On the exhibition walls, Arabic occupies the right and English the left, their opposing reading directions approaching a shared centre. Neither feels secondary. Within the artworks, handwriting retains the irregular rhythm of an individual gesture, while stencilled lettering introduces repetition and control. The connected curves of Arabic encounter the separated forms of Latin letters. Meaning travels between languages and materials without always requiring translation.

In the suspended Beyond the Page (2026), these relationships become physical. Its irregular silhouette, stitched construction, eyelets and exposed fastenings recall American sculptor Lee Bontecou, whose canvas-and-steel reliefs similarly made seams and openings integral to their compositions. Walking around Al Sowaidi’s work reveals another surface of handwritten thoughts, ruled lines and visible stitching. Both sides contribute to the composition. A line can record a thought, join two pieces of fabric or mark where something has been cut away.

Elsewhere, the journal expands into architecture. In Still Attached (2026), suspended painted textiles create passages through which visitors move, their shapes briefly aligning before separating again. Layers of Us (2026)introduces overlapping surfaces and circular openings that rearrange the composition as perspectives shift. In Sophisticated Storm , angular forms occupy a corner and spill onto the floor, incorporating mirrored fragments. At certain angles, an opening frames a window or another painted surface. Move a few steps and the composition disappears. Shadows, floor patterns and architectural details become newly apparent. The works encourage attention to spaces that might otherwise remain unnoticed.

Yet the exhibition is less assured in its earlier rooms, where the abundance of paintings, textiles and smaller works occasionally fragments an otherwise coherent visual language. The later installations benefit from greater concentration, allowing individual ideas to occupy entire spaces. The translucent floral works of Secret Garden , though delicate, remain more contained within their room, without the same engagement with the surrounding architecture.

A nearby film offers an intriguing counterpoint. Showing Al Sowaidi writing, painting, cutting and rearranging materials, it reveals the labour behind the exhibition’s forms. Its looping structure reinforces the idea of an unfinished journal. In the room of repeated Arabic and English phrases, a paint-covered studio table holds a small fabric fragment bearing the words ‘Restless Calm’. Against the surrounding accumulation, the isolated phrase gains particular presence.

The film also observes that not everything that grows needs to be seen, a sentiment that acquires an unintended curatorial resonance. A more selective presentation might have allowed some of the earlier works greater space to breathe. At times, the poetic wall statements similarly explain emotions that the materials communicate more effectively.

Outside, Remains of Wonder (2026) returns the recurring shapes to the courtyard. Freestanding panels frame foliage, windows and fragments of the surrounding architecture. Openings in the artworks begin to resemble those in the buildings, while spaces between branches echo the contours encountered inside. What initially appeared to be an unfamiliar alphabet has become a way of seeing. Al Sowaidi’s journal extends beyond its pages, changing how the surrounding world is read.

A Journal of Becoming runs until 23 November

article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Penélope Cruz had been a muse to Los Javis — the moniker for Spanish filmmakers Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo — for years before they met for lunch to persuade her to play a singer (more a force of nature, really) in La Bola Negra , an electrifying sensation at Cannes that’s now Spain’s entry for best international feature film Oscar .", "links": [{"text": "Penélope Cruz", "url": "https://deadline.com/tag/penelope-cruz-2/"}, {"text": "Los Javis", "url": "https://deadline.com/tag/los-javis/"}, {"text": "La Bola Negra", "url": "https://deadline.com/tag/la-bola-negra/"}, {"text": "Spain’s entry for best international feature film Oscar", "url": "https://deadline.com/lists/oscars-2027-international-feature-film-submissions/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“I saw her in a clip of Jamón Jamón ,” says Ambrossi, referring to Bigas Luna’s 1992 picture, in which Cruz appeared for the first time opposite her now-husband Javier Bardem. “I was young, and I thought, ‘Who is she ?!’ ”"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Related Stories"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/200723.jpg?w=300", "alt": "‘La Bola Negra’", "caption": "", "credit": "Deadline · Film"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "‘La Bola Negra’ Review: Spain’s Javier Calvo And Javier Ambrossi Capture Hearts With Their Unashamedly Romantic Decades-Spanning Drama – Cannes Film Festival", "links": [{"text": "‘La Bola Negra’ Review: Spain’s Javier Calvo And Javier Ambrossi Capture Hearts With Their Unashamedly Romantic Decades-Spanning Drama – Cannes Film Festival", "url": "https://deadline.com/2026/05/la-bola-negra-review-javier-calvo-and-javier-ambrossi-penelope-cruz-1236918715/"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/La-Bola-Negra-Cannes.jpg?w=300", "alt": "CANNES, FRANCE - (Photo by Kate Green/Getty Images)", "caption": "", "credit": "Deadline · Film"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Penélope Cruz’s ‘La Bola Negra’ Lands 20-Minute Ovation From Overjoyed Audience At Cannes", "links": [{"text": "Penélope Cruz’s ‘La Bola Negra’ Lands 20-Minute Ovation From Overjoyed Audience At Cannes", "url": "https://deadline.com/2026/05/la-bola-negra-cannes-ovation-penelope-cruz-1236917575/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Calvo was similarly enchanted when he saw Cruz in Pedro Almodóvar’s 1999 Oscar winner All About My Mother . “She’s got that material of the stars,” he says. “When you put a camera in front of her, she can do anything, and she doesn’t even realize what she’s doing. There’s a power , there’s a force guiding her, and that’s amazing to see first-hand.”"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Watch on Deadline"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Los Javis wanted Cruz for a small but pivotal role in their epic tale La Bola Negra , the intertwined story of three gay men who exist in three different time periods in Spain. In 1932, Carlos (Milo Quifes) is a young man in Grenada at a time when Spain is lurching uncomfortably towards an ever-increasing spiteful intolerance of homosexuality. In 1937, against the backdrop of the Spanish Civil War, Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) and Rafael ( Miguel Bernardeau ) are soldiers from opposing political divides brought closer by the conflict. And in 2017, Alberto (Carlos González) is a playwright from Madrid who engages with an eminent Federico Garcia Lorca scholar (played by another Hollywood star, Glenn Close , speaking fluent Spanish) in a storyline that links the characters in the prior timelines.", "links": [{"text": "Miguel Bernardeau", "url": "https://deadline.com/tag/miguel-bernardeau/"}, {"text": "Glenn Close", "url": "https://deadline.com/tag/glenn-close/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "RELATED: Netflix Unveils U.S. Market Rollout For ‘La Bola Negra’ Theatrical Release", "links": [{"text": "Netflix Unveils U.S. Market Rollout For ‘La Bola Negra’ Theatrical Release", "url": "https://deadline.com/2026/09/netflix-la-bola-negra-markets-box-office-1237073639/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Cruz’s character, one Nené Romero, performs for the troops in a series of beautifully choreographed, risqué numbers that the boys, far from home, lap up with hunger in their eyes. Los Javis say that Nené was inspired by La Fornarina, a cupletista , a Spanish singer of cuplé songs — bawdy numbers about “sex and drugs,” as Calvo explains it — who performed in theaters in Madrid around the turn of the last century."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Their research included the study of the erotic novels penned by Spanish writer and fashion designer Álvaro Retana, who also wrote lyrics for saucy songs of the type that Cruz performs in La Bola Negra . “They would be singing all over Madrid. They were so funny, they were unleashed — and they thought they were going to be free forever,” says Calvo when we meet in a suite at the swanky Corinthia Hotel during the London Film Festival. “But these singers and their gay friends, all the people in that circle, they were all incarcerated, persecuted, killed or disappeared. They’re forgotten, kind of. So we wanted to bring them back.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Cruz was already a fan of Los Javis having been gripped by their outrageously captivating 2023 TV drama miniseries La Mesías , a hit for Moviestar+ in Spain, which is now available via Mubi in the UK, Canada Turkey, the Netherlands, Germany and Australia, and will soon be streaming in France. “They are so talented,” I recall an ecstatic Cruz telling me at the closing-night party in Cannes. “I saw their first television show Veneno as well,” she said, “and now they’ve won the directing prize at Cannes .”", "links": [{"text": "won the directing prize at Cannes", "url": "https://deadline.com/2026/05/cannes-2026-winners-live-updating-1236919837/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The next time they work with Cruz, says Ambrossi, they plan to create “a whole film around her,” but that will be be after what they hope will be their next feature project, a movie that they claim will be “90% in English.” That movie, whenever it’s made, will likely have a larger budget than Los Javis spent on La Bola Negra . Ambrossi says that its roughly $15 million budget was tight but it’s “big for a Spanish movie.”"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/La-Bola-Negra_Group00841.jpg?w=300", "alt": "The 'La Bola Negra’ team at TIFF ", "caption": "The ‘La Bola Negra’ team at the Deadline Studio during the Toronto Film Festival Deadline", "credit": "Deadline · Film"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "With time and the right people on La Bola Negra , Ambrossi adds, “we knew we could do it big. The scope is not always about big landscapes; it’s about how you position people, so you get the sense that it’s bigger, and taking the time to find the right locations, because these are all natural locations.“ They also insisted on making time for proper rehearsals before the 12-week shoot (“Because it’s a deep story and the actors needed time”)."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Calvo explains that with the purse strings being so tight they had to find “creative solutions.” They didn’t, for example, have a room in which to shoot all the soldiers having dinner. “We’re like, “OK, then we’ll compose a beautiful shot with everyone outside with tables, and we’ll just imagine they went out to have dinner there,” he explains."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "They also turned to “the godfathers of cinema,” as Calvo refers to such legendary directors as Thodōros Angelopoulos ( Alexander the Great ) and Andrei Tarkovsky ( Solaris ), who, “with just with a landscape, mist and composing the humans in a proper way” were able to conjure up scenes of movie magic."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Working with the sublime cinematographer Gris Jordana — a frequent collaborator, as are the film’s editor, production designer, hair and makeup designer, costume designer, composer, and many other key creatives — Los Javis sought to bring some of that “godfathers of cinema” magic to their own film. “They’re part of our team,” Amborossi says. “We have been growing together. In every project we learn together. So that’s why the movie is so big, even if the budget is not. They put a lot of effort because it’s a collective experience. It’s like they put in their souls.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“This is a movie about poetry,” says Calvo, “and there’s also a poetry in images. You don’t have to show everything. You can give something, and the viewer will leave it to their imagination.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "RELATED: ‘La Bola Negra’ Directors Dig Into Generational Trauma: “Something Touched Deep Inside” – Contenders London", "links": [{"text": "‘La Bola Negra’ Directors Dig Into Generational Trauma: “Something Touched Deep Inside” – Contenders London", "url": "https://deadline.com/2026/10/la-bola-negra-generational-trauma-contenders-london-1237151053/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Ambrosssi jumps in. “If you don’t have the money, just don’t do it badly,” he says. “Cut it, and someone can talk about it in the next scene. Sometimes we needed a natural beauty location. For example, we didn’t have an office for the general lieutenant featured in the film, so we found an empty space with a nice view — you can see the sea — and we composed it with people and a table and a small framed picture of Franco, and that was it. article_text:
Penélope Cruz had been a muse to Los Javis — the moniker for Spanish filmmakers Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo — for years before they met for lunch to persuade her to play a singer (more a force of nature, really) in La Bola Negra , an electrifying sensation at Cannes that’s now Spain’s entry for best international feature film Oscar .

“I saw her in a clip of Jamón Jamón ,” says Ambrossi, referring to Bigas Luna’s 1992 picture, in which Cruz appeared for the first time opposite her now-husband Javier Bardem. “I was young, and I thought, ‘Who is she ?!’ ”

Related Stories

‘La Bola Negra’ Review: Spain’s Javier Calvo And Javier Ambrossi Capture Hearts With Their Unashamedly Romantic Decades-Spanning Drama – Cannes Film Festival

Penélope Cruz’s ‘La Bola Negra’ Lands 20-Minute Ovation From Overjoyed Audience At Cannes

Calvo was similarly enchanted when he saw Cruz in Pedro Almodóvar’s 1999 Oscar winner All About My Mother . “She’s got that material of the stars,” he says. “When you put a camera in front of her, she can do anything, and she doesn’t even realize what she’s doing. There’s a power , there’s a force guiding her, and that’s amazing to see first-hand.”

Watch on Deadline

Los Javis wanted Cruz for a small but pivotal role in their epic tale La Bola Negra , the intertwined story of three gay men who exist in three different time periods in Spain. In 1932, Carlos (Milo Quifes) is a young man in Grenada at a time when Spain is lurching uncomfortably towards an ever-increasing spiteful intolerance of homosexuality. In 1937, against the backdrop of the Spanish Civil War, Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) and Rafael ( Miguel Bernardeau ) are soldiers from opposing political divides brought closer by the conflict. And in 2017, Alberto (Carlos González) is a playwright from Madrid who engages with an eminent Federico Garcia Lorca scholar (played by another Hollywood star, Glenn Close , speaking fluent Spanish) in a storyline that links the characters in the prior timelines.

RELATED: Netflix Unveils U.S. Market Rollout For ‘La Bola Negra’ Theatrical Release

Cruz’s character, one Nené Romero, performs for the troops in a series of beautifully choreographed, risqué numbers that the boys, far from home, lap up with hunger in their eyes. Los Javis say that Nené was inspired by La Fornarina, a cupletista , a Spanish singer of cuplé songs — bawdy numbers about “sex and drugs,” as Calvo explains it — who performed in theaters in Madrid around the turn of the last century.

Their research included the study of the erotic novels penned by Spanish writer and fashion designer Álvaro Retana, who also wrote lyrics for saucy songs of the type that Cruz performs in La Bola Negra . “They would be singing all over Madrid. They were so funny, they were unleashed — and they thought they were going to be free forever,” says Calvo when we meet in a suite at the swanky Corinthia Hotel during the London Film Festival. “But these singers and their gay friends, all the people in that circle, they were all incarcerated, persecuted, killed or disappeared. They’re forgotten, kind of. So we wanted to bring them back.”

Cruz was already a fan of Los Javis having been gripped by their outrageously captivating 2023 TV drama miniseries La Mesías , a hit for Moviestar+ in Spain, which is now available via Mubi in the UK, Canada Turkey, the Netherlands, Germany and Australia, and will soon be streaming in France. “They are so talented,” I recall an ecstatic Cruz telling me at the closing-night party in Cannes. “I saw their first television show Veneno as well,” she said, “and now they’ve won the directing prize at Cannes .”

The next time they work with Cruz, says Ambrossi, they plan to create “a whole film around her,” but that will be be after what they hope will be their next feature project, a movie that they claim will be “90% in English.” That movie, whenever it’s made, will likely have a larger budget than Los Javis spent on La Bola Negra . Ambrossi says that its roughly $15 million budget was tight but it’s “big for a Spanish movie.”

With time and the right people on La Bola Negra , Ambrossi adds, “we knew we could do it big. The scope is not always about big landscapes; it’s about how you position people, so you get the sense that it’s bigger, and taking the time to find the right locations, because these are all natural locations.“ They also insisted on making time for proper rehearsals before the 12-week shoot (“Because it’s a deep story and the actors needed time”).

Calvo explains that with the purse strings being so tight they had to find “creative solutions.” They didn’t, for example, have a room in which to shoot all the soldiers having dinner. “We’re like, “OK, then we’ll compose a beautiful shot with everyone outside with tables, and we’ll just imagine they went out to have dinner there,” he explains.

They also turned to “the godfathers of cinema,” as Calvo refers to such legendary directors as Thodōros Angelopoulos ( Alexander the Great ) and Andrei Tarkovsky ( Solaris ), who, “with just with a landscape, mist and composing the humans in a proper way” were able to conjure up scenes of movie magic.

Working with the sublime cinematographer Gris Jordana — a frequent collaborator, as are the film’s editor, production designer, hair and makeup designer, costume designer, composer, and many other key creatives — Los Javis sought to bring some of that “godfathers of cinema” magic to their own film. “They’re part of our team,” Amborossi says. “We have been growing together. In every project we learn together. So that’s why the movie is so big, even if the budget is not. They put a lot of effort because it’s a collective experience. It’s like they put in their souls.”

“This is a movie about poetry,” says Calvo, “and there’s also a poetry in images. You don’t have to show everything. You can give something, and the viewer will leave it to their imagination.”

RELATED: ‘La Bola Negra’ Directors Dig Into Generational Trauma: “Something Touched Deep Inside” – Contenders London

Ambrosssi jumps in. “If you don’t have the money, just don’t do it badly,” he says. “Cut it, and someone can talk about it in the next scene. Sometimes we needed a natural beauty location. For example, we didn’t have an office for the general lieutenant featured in the film, so we found an empty space with a nice view — you can see the sea — and we composed it with people and a table and a small framed picture of Franco, and that was it. And that’s not expensive.”

The main point, Calvo believes — as the likes of David Lean found while directing Lawrence of Arabia — is that it was necessary to find intimacy within such an epic story.

Los Javis were helped in that endeavor, Calvo adds, because the film is loosely based on Alberto Conejero’s one-act play La Piedra Oscura , which deals only with the relationship between Rafael and Sebastian, a play that is “so intimate and delicate” that they wanted to expand it into a triptych. ”Like, a big movie,” says Calvo, spreading his arms wide, “and an intimate movie at the same time. You have the fragility and the the war, so it’s about contrast. And it was so nice to create that, because sometimes it’s more difficult to create the relationship of Rafael and Sebastian, with all the tension, than a bombing scene.”

Countless meetings with key creatives were held in pre-production to map out the movie, and the more mistakes they made the better, because it meant they’d go out and get it right during the shoot, says Ambrossi. “It’s like, work, work, work, work, make a mistake, then try again,” he says, smiling. The work, however, didn’t feel like work. ”I always go back and say, ‘Oh, wow, it was the journey of our lives,’” Calvo declares.

RELATED: Netflix Enters Box Office Era With ‘La Bola Negra’; ‘You Can See Everything’ & ‘Musk’ Face Off – Specialty Preview

Ambrossi contends that the film is proudly gay, whether that puts it in a niche box or not; it’s “a gay movie” and “I love to keep it that way,” he says. “I want people to have an experience that is universal. But I don’t want them to miss that it’s gay.”

It’s certainly unusual to see a gay story against the backdrop of war. Calvo cites Tarkovsky’s classic Ivan’s Childhood , Elem Klimov’s harrowing Come and See and Francis Ford Coppola’s Apocalypse Now as being amongst his favorite war movies. “So, I have those references,” he says, “but my emotion is another thing, and my sensitivity is what we’re portraying. Why shouldn’t I make a movie the same way the people that made war movies I admire made, but telling my own story and using my own feelings? For me, it was natural to just talk about myself through my references. And why can’t we have it all?”

Ambrossi laughs. “It’s great that we told everyone it is a gay film with — mostly — gay actors portraying gay characters, directed by gay people about the queer experience, and it’s hitting the No. 1 spot at the box office every single night in Spain. I like that. I think it’s cool, because it really represents two things; one, that the world is going in a direction that we are not always aware, and also that the industry has to understand that gay stories are not niche.”

La Bola Negra is a starting point for the next conversation, Ambrosssi continues, and that “once we try, once we prove them wrong, then we can have the conversation about universal stories. But we had to tell them, ‘You don’t have to change the lead and put a straight star in it to get the audience.’ They just go, “Ah, it’s a gay story.’”

Were they pressured in any way to compromise? “They don’t even try to do it with us, because we write, direct and produce. It’s our movie,” Ambrossi responds with gusto. He allows, however, that they encountered difficulties making the 2020 miniseries Veneno . “It was a show with trans actresses, and everyone was like, ‘You won’t find that many trans actresses to put in a show in Spain.’ And we were like, ‘We’ll do it.’ And we did.”

RELATED: ‘La Bola Negra’s Los Javis On Completing The Final Work Of Gay Poet “Murdered By Fascism” In 1936 Spain — Toronto Studio

During their travels promoting the movie — at Cannes (where Los Javis shared the best director prize with Fatherland’s Pawel Pawlikowski), Telluride, Toronto (where it won the People’s Choice Award for best film), San Sebastián (where the film was honored with the festival’s Audience Award) and here in London — the reaction has been overwhelmingly positive. “The feedback from non-gay people, non-LGBTQ people, is the same. This idea of wanting to be yourself, being rejected, a lot of women get that. It gets everyone. At some point, it’s about family, about motherhood, about brotherhood, about friendship. It’s a war movie. It’s about being different, but it’s about art and the power of art.”

Calvo, listening intently, jumps in, pointing out that the film is “about understanding and seeing the other as a human being. Which is, I think, important.”

xxx

When it came to casting the male leads, they chose singer-musician Guitarricadelafuente because they were drawn to the “magnetism, the sadness” in his eyes. “He had to be the eyes of the viewer,” says Calvo, “and he has eyes that you can rely on, and he had this shyness, but also this bravery, this strength, but then this subtleness. We just knew it was for him.”

Ambrossi, meanwhile, hails Bernardeau ( Elite ) as being “one of the best of his generation.” “We needed his technique,” he explains, “because Guitarricadelafuente is new, so we needed the balance to play off each other.” The same goes for González. “He’s so flamboyant and fun in real life,” Ambrossi says. “Here, he’s doing a job that you cannot imagine. If you were to meet him, you would be like, ‘Are you the same person ?’”

Indeed, I spoke with González at a soirée following a special screening of La Bola Negra at Tate Modern, and he was an absolute hoot. He vowed to do anything for the film “with its big black balls.” My eyes widened at that remark and our dirty laughter nearly got us turned outta the party.

As for Carlos, they were looking for Andalusian guys, and the moment they saw Quifes’ audition, they shut down the search.

The roles played by Guitarricadelafuente and Bernardeau are the heart of the film, providing its most tender, heartfelt moments. They met for the first time at rehearsals, where Guitarricadelfuente, who’d never acted before, says he felt “100 percent safe” because he was working opposite a professional actor. “It was a very special moment meeting Miguel,” he says.

Having someone like Miguel “really helped me out in this in this journey,” Guitarricadelafuente says. “There was something very special about the way that our characters grew up together, and the development of that intimacy, that way of nonverbal communication, those gestures that communicated so much. I’m grateful for the time that we spent at that room rehearsing.”

Los Javis were “democratic with us,” he notes, because “they let us express ourselves freely, and if there was maybe sometimes in the dialogue something that maybe didn’t resound that much in ourselves, they would say, ‘What would you say? What would you do?’ They let us roll on and magical things happened.”

Were they able to improvise? Bernardeau shakes his head and notes that it wasn’t so much improvisation because of how much thought went into every scene, what with how the three stories intertwine. “You need to be careful with what you change. There’s a lot of detail, so you cannot improvise. But they were very free with us in changing smaller stuff. I did feel very free to try different ways and paths into the scenes.”

I remember covering the film’s ecstatic 20-minute ovation at Cannes in the Grand Théâtre Lumière and watching the faces of this new generation of filmmakers and actors. Bernardeau was holding back tears. “I knew that once I start crying I would not stop,” he admits.

In front of him, he recalls, was the festival’s camera team “and Tilda Swinton clapping and looking at us.” Swinton introduced Bernardeau to her agent Christian Hodell, chief executive of Hamilton Hodell, who now represents him. Now the actor will soon be moving from Spain to live in London.

Guitarricadelafuente remembers looking up to the Lumière’s second tier to see so many young people who’d clearly connected with the film: “That made me feel as if we were at a concert.” He notes that he’s been astonished by how audiences in Spain have flocked to see the picture. Los Javis were known to young people, he says. “Like, there are people in my family that haven’t been to the cinema in 10 years. They feel like they’re missing out on something, because there’s been like a consensus between everybody to see it. It’s not a film about civil war, it’s not a film about Lorca. It’s is a film about life.”

It sure is.

Culturally, Spain’s on a roll. Singer-songwriter Rosalía took the International Artist of the Year at the Brit Awards; La Bola Negra won a major prize at Cannes; and, of course, Spain won the World Cup. Calvo beams a full-wattage smile. “We’re just getting out there.”

Netflix releases the film in theaters Friday in New York City and Los Angeles ahead of a wider release over coming weeks before debuting on streaming in the U.S. and Canada on December 2. Altitude opens the film in the UK on November 6.

With his previous feature, Armageddon Time , the wizened filmmaker—whose borne the reputation as a deeply humane screenwriter, quietly piercing storyteller, and cinematic historian of his birthplace and Jewish-Russian heritage—returned with a family drama fit for even the most tender audiences. He’s the kind of confident, wheeling-and-dealing socialite who can casually afford to have Peter Luger deliver a porterhouse for six to the suburban outreaches of Queens’ 75th street in Jackson Heights—a few miles from where Gray grew up in Flushing, and where Gary’s civil-engineer brother Irwin (Miles Teller) lives a more humble family life with his wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) and two teenage sons Scott and Ben (Gavin Goudey and Roman Engel). The Russian mob renders moot the socio-political dynamic of the ‘60s and ‘70s in which Gary still operates. But he’s too used to the old game to see that the paper tiger is not made of paper after all; rather, an imported steel the likes of which he can’t imagine."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "And it doesn’t matter how hard Irwin tries to stay out of Gary’s business dealings. But one can tell by Irwin’s demeanor that he’s never dealt with any kind of mob. That’s until Gary arrives with a consulting engineering pitch for cleaning up the Gowanus Canal, Brooklyn’s most polluted waterway for more than 100 years. The only problem? The Russians own it now."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "What starts as a congenial deal between the brothers and Russians devolves into chaos when Irwin innocently shows up at the canal with his two boys one night to teach them a little something about his line of work, only to discover the goons dumping oil. article_text:
Note: This review was originally published as part of our 2026 Cannes coverage. The film arrives in theaters on November 13.

James Gray had left the comfort zone of the native New York he chronicled over the first two decades of his career, sending Charlie Hunnam, Robert Pattinson, and Tom Holland into the Amazon jungle for The Lost City of Z and launching Brad Pitt into space with Ad Astra . With his previous feature, Armageddon Time , the wizened filmmaker—whose borne the reputation as a deeply humane screenwriter, quietly piercing storyteller, and cinematic historian of his birthplace and Jewish-Russian heritage—returned with a family drama fit for even the most tender audiences. With his newest, Paper Tiger , he returns to the roots planted in his first three films ( Little Odessa , The Yards , We Own the Night ): gritty, mafia-ridden crime in the Empire City’s fabled underworld.

Gary Pearl (Adam Driver) is a divorced, retired NYPD cop who wields his backing from the powerful, shady municipal institution to turn a much larger profit from security advising for whoever has the money to hire him. He’s the kind of confident, wheeling-and-dealing socialite who can casually afford to have Peter Luger deliver a porterhouse for six to the suburban outreaches of Queens’ 75th street in Jackson Heights—a few miles from where Gray grew up in Flushing, and where Gary’s civil-engineer brother Irwin (Miles Teller) lives a more humble family life with his wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) and two teenage sons Scott and Ben (Gavin Goudey and Roman Engel). This is a Jewish family neither involved in nor looking for trouble.

But it doesn’t matter who Gary is, how much money he has, or what kind of leverage he touts across the city. A new era of mob life is arising at the height of the Cold War in 1986 south and central Brooklyn, where the Russian mafia arrives in droves to brutally establish a new order of respect and rule-making that goes beyond the NYPD, the old-guard Italian mafia, and any other prominent Gothamites that ran the city behind closed doors. The Russian mob renders moot the socio-political dynamic of the ‘60s and ‘70s in which Gary still operates. But he’s too used to the old game to see that the paper tiger is not made of paper after all; rather, an imported steel the likes of which he can’t imagine.

And it doesn’t matter how hard Irwin tries to stay out of Gary’s business dealings. Gary is too smooth, self-assured, and fast for Irwin, who you can tell has spent a lifetime caving to his older brother’s wishes, which always come with a gift in tow (a new car, $10,000, etc.) accompanied by Gary’s lovable, sweethearted nature, which seems genuinely hard to reject. But one can tell by Irwin’s demeanor that he’s never dealt with any kind of mob. That’s until Gary arrives with a consulting engineering pitch for cleaning up the Gowanus Canal, Brooklyn’s most polluted waterway for more than 100 years. The only problem? The Russians own it now.

What starts as a congenial deal between the brothers and Russians devolves into chaos when Irwin innocently shows up at the canal with his two boys one night to teach them a little something about his line of work, only to discover the goons dumping oil. This incidentally stirs a whole heap of trouble that Gary can only fix through ruthless mob boss Simeon Bogoyavich (Victor Ptak). Meanwhile, Hester wrestles alone with sudden health issues that threaten to unroot her crucial role in the Pearl family. What unfolds is a masterfully measured, character-driven, quintessentially subtle James Gray mob picture.

A real where’s-where of south and central Brooklyn replete with iconic restaurants, bars, and neighborhoods (something any New Yorker or New York-lover is bound to get giddy over), Paper Tiger isn’t quite the triumph that Gray managed in similarly set and themed work ( The Yards still wears that gold, with We Own the Night taking silver), yet it’s certainly something to behold, the type of film that doesn’t take things so far as desired while lingering still. It plants seeds of lavish characterization, heart-wrenching drama, and gutting tension that leaves one thinking about these people, these places, and the world we live in with a raw sting, as if all of it, down to the bone, is culled directly from history, not a single shrewd detail made up.

Driver, Teller, and Johansson are all equally fantastic under the direction of Gray and his brilliant screenplay. Joaquín Baca-Asay––returning after We Own the Night and Two Lovers–– delivers an inspired vintage aesthetic that draws out Gray’s now-retro directorial tendencies (read: the opposite of a Netflix movie). Wardrobes and sets feel more found than created, a testament to the work of costume designer Amy Roth and production designer Happy Massee.

All said, a few elements dangle. Scott Morris’ edit, which could’ve used another pass, carries moments of deadweight. And while the ending is engrossing, one can’t help noticing that it’s a bit uninspired, copied directly from one of the most prominent crime films of all time, and nearly plagiarizing one of his own. Yet Paper Tiger is a welcome addition to the oeuvre and one that has potential to mature into something even greater. The man simply knows how to tell a New York story.

Paper Tiger premiered at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival and will be released by NEON.

title_original: Don’t Forget the Other ‘Heat’ Movie, Which Gave Burt Reynolds One of His Best Noir Roles
editorial_title_zh: 别忘了另一部《Heat》，它为伯特·雷诺兹带来了他最好的黑色电影角色之一
editorial_excerpt_zh: 这部硬汉派佳作改编自传奇编剧威廉·戈德曼的剧本，几乎在一上映就被不公正地遗忘了。它的40周年纪念提供了一个改变这一现状的机会。

"埃斯卡兰特试图通过帮助一名遭受虐待狂年轻黑帮毒打的受害者来寻求道德救赎的故事，在犀利的机智（包涵戈德曼写过的最棒的台词——对于一个写过《虎豹小霸王》的人来说，这已经很不容易了）与沉思般的自我审视场景之间切换，同时穿插着令人震惊、编排精妙的暴力爆发和惆怅的浪漫情愫。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拉斯维加斯的背景为这一切增添了更多层的讽刺与共鸣，这个地方似乎在嘲弄埃斯卡兰特发大财并隐退到意大利安度晚年的梦想，而戈德曼选择将电影背景设定在圣诞节，则对埃斯卡兰特进行了更残酷的嘲弄。尽管《热点》是戈德曼知名度最低的电影之一（在备受推崇的《总统班底》、《马拉松人》和《危情十日》的光芒下，它很容易被遗忘），但它也是他笔触最优美的作品之一，其中的俏皮话既妙语连珠又发人深省，其交织的剧情所带来的情感冲击确实会悄然潜入你的心底。", "随着电影导演本人在媒体上唱衰影片，《烈焰悍将》从一开始就毫无胜算。然而，成片并未显现出任何制作失调的迹象，除了略显突兀和简短的结局（这是拍摄的多个结局之一）之外。归根结底，威廉·戈德曼和伯特·雷诺兹——而非任何一位导演——才是《烈焰悍将》真正的作者；他们对尼克·埃斯卡兰特这一尊严受损、自我毁灭、浪漫深情、备受煎熬且可能难逃厄运的英雄形象的构思始终如一，赋予了《烈焰悍将》持久的情感共鸣与力量，时隔40年依然历久弥新。", Card）。尽管戈德曼再度亲自操刀剧本，该版本同样未能打动影评人或观众。事已至此，我们不难认为《烈焰悍将》或许注定是一部命运多舛的项目——这实在令人惋惜，因为它恰好代表了戈德曼最具艺术水准的巅峰时刻之一。", "translated": true}]
